scenarios.guidance:
This scenario is the flow itself — it walks the journey end-to-end and is what Kerno calibrates on. It must not be removed.

The owner Ada North raises the spending limit on her seeded debit card and reads it back. Mint Ada's access token in arrange with `AuthClient.getTokenByPassword` from `@auth0/auth0-auth-js` (never `mintJwt`, never a hand-rolled `POST /oauth/token`), reading `AUTH0_DOMAIN` (hostname only, `localhost:3000`), `AUTH0_CLIENT_ID`, `AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET`, `AUTH0_AUDIENCE`, `AUTH0_TEST_USERNAME`, `AUTH0_TEST_PASSWORD`; a token failure caused by the client requesting `https://` against this HTTP-only local issuer is an environment fault — report BLOCKED, not an endpoint defect. Then walk three MCP `tools/call` requests with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`: `list_cards` (setup — locate card `10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000041`, last four `4412`, and capture its current limit), `set_card_limit` (the change — a fresh positive integer minor amount generated for this run and different from the current one), and `list_cards` again (the step the flow is ABOUT — the card must now report the limit Ada set). The final `list_cards` response is the one asserted in full: tool success, and the card entry's every field (`id`, `memberId`, `accountId`, `lastFour`, `status`, `spendingLimitMinor`, `currency`) accounted for, with `spendingLimitMinor` equal to the amount sent in step 2. Cleanup restores `spending_limit_minor` to the seeded 500000 by writing the `cards` row directly over `DATABASE_URL` and verifying the update affected exactly one row.

spec.title: The owner changes her debit card's spending limit and sees the new limit when she lists her cards
preconditions: The Northwharf MCP server is reachable and serves stateless `tools/call` requests at the SUT MCP endpoint.

Ada North exists as an owner member of Northwharf Ltd (`10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001`) and an access token minted for her by the local Auth0 issuer via the password grant carries `cards:read` and `cards:manage`.
The seeded card `10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000041` (last four `4412`) exists for that organization.
spec.trigger: Ada calls `tools/call list_cards`, then `tools/call set_card_limit` with `{ cardId: "10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000041", spendingLimitMinor: <fresh positive integer generated for this run, different from the limit observed in step 1> }`, then `tools/call list_cards` again — every call carrying `Authorization: Bearer <Ada's access token>`.
mainSuccessScenario: `TOOL list_cards` — Ada lists the organization's cards; the call succeeds and the response contains an entry whose `id` is `10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000041`. Capture that entry's `spendingLimitMinor` as the pre-change limit and its `memberId`, `accountId`, `lastFour`, `status` and `currency` as the values the change must leave untouched.

`TOOL set_card_limit` — Ada sets that card's `spendingLimitMinor` to the fresh per-run amount; the call succeeds (not an MCP tool error) and the returned card's `id` and `spendingLimitMinor` are the ones sent.
`TOOL list_cards` — Ada lists the cards again and reads the card back; this is the step the flow is about and its response is asserted in full.
postconditions: Step 1 (`list_cards`, fixture): the tool call succeeded — the result is not an MCP tool error — and its parsed `cards` array contains exactly one entry whose `id` is `10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000041`; that entry's `spendingLimitMinor` is an integer (the pre-change limit the flow carries forward).

Step 2 (`set_card_limit`, fixture): the tool call succeeded — the result is not an MCP tool error — and the parsed card's `id` equals the `cardId` sent and its `spendingLimitMinor` equals the `spendingLimitMinor` sent.

Step 3, outcome: the final `list_cards` result is not an MCP tool error (`isError` is not true) and its `content` is a single `{ type: "text" }` entry whose `text` parses as JSON with exactly the key `cards`, an array.
Step 3, outcome: the final `cards` array contains exactly one entry with `id` `10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000041`.
Step 3, the business outcome the user named: that entry's `spendingLimitMinor` equals the `spendingLimitMinor` sent in step 2, and is NOT the pre-change limit captured in step 1.

Step 3, field accounting for that card entry — the entry equals exactly `{ id, memberId, accountId, lastFour, status, spendingLimitMinor, currency }` with: `id` equal to `10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000041`; `memberId` equal to the `memberId` seen in step 1 (a UUID string); `accountId` equal to the `accountId` seen in step 1 (a UUID string); `lastFour` equal to `"4412"`; `status` equal to the `status` seen in step 1 and a member of `["active", "frozen", "cancelled"]`; `spendingLimitMinor` the amount sent in step 2; `currency` equal to the `currency` seen in step 1 and a member of `["GBP", "EUR", "USD"]`. No other key is present on the entry.

Step 3, response headers: the HTTP response headers of the final `tools/call` match the observed baseline — pin `Content-Type` as observed (the MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint answers `application/json` or `text/event-stream`), and pin as absent any of `Cache-Control`, `Vary`, `Set-Cookie`, `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, `Content-Security-Policy`, `Strict-Transport-Security`, `X-Frame-Options`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy` the endpoint does not send. If the MCP client used to make the call does not expose response headers, record that as a declared gap in the finding rather than inventing values. Never assert `Date`, `Content-Length`, `ETag` or trace ids.

Persisted state: the `cards` row with `id = '10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000041'` has `spending_limit_minor` equal to the amount sent in step 2 and `organization_id` `10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001`.
spec.primaryActor: Ada North, the seeded owner of Northwharf Ltd (subject `auth0|6728f0a1b2c3d4e5f6789012`)
spec.scope: FLOW owner-changes-a-card-limit (TOOL list_cards → TOOL set_card_limit → TOOL list_cards)
cleanup: Restore the seeded limit: `UPDATE cards SET spending_limit_minor = 500000 WHERE id = '10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000041'`, asserting `rowCount` is 1.
Close the Postgres connection (`await db.end().catch(() => {})` inside a `finally`).
spec.notes:
The MCP tool layer reports business failures as a tool result with `isError: true` and a `{ error, message }` JSON text body rather than a non-2xx HTTP status, so success is judged on `isError`/the parsed payload, not on the HTTP status alone.

The card under test is seeded and shared — there is no way to create a fresh card through the exposed tools. Use a fresh per-run `spendingLimitMinor` (e.g. a random integer in a band well away from 500000) so the asserted value is distinct from the seeded one, and restore 500000 in cleanup. Two concurrent runs of this flow against the same card would interfere; that is inherent to a single seeded fixture row and is noted rather than engineered around.

The card entry's field list is taken from `toCard` in `src/db/store.ts` (`id`, `memberId`, `accountId`, `lastFour`, `status`, `spendingLimitMinor`, `currency`); the enum sets come from the `cards_status` and `cards_currency` CHECK constraints in `drizzle/0000_lovely_bug.sql`.

precondition.description:
The Northwharf MCP server is deployed and reachable at the SUT base URL (the Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint, `POST /mcp`), and answers stateless `tools/call` requests with `content-type: application/json` and `accept: application/json, text/event-stream`.

The local Auth0 stand-in issuer is reachable and can mint an owner access token: `AUTH0_DOMAIN` (hostname only, `localhost:3000`), `AUTH0_CLIENT_ID`, `AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET`, `AUTH0_AUDIENCE`, `AUTH0_TEST_USERNAME` and `AUTH0_TEST_PASSWORD` are all present in the environment, and `AuthClient.getTokenByPassword` from `@auth0/auth0-auth-js` returns an access token for the seeded owner Ada North (subject `auth0|6728f0a1b2c3d4e5f6789012`) carrying the full owner permission set, including `cards:read` and `cards:manage`. `AuthClient` always requests `https://AUTH0_DOMAIN` while this issuer listens over plain HTTP on port 3000 — a token request that fails for that reason is an ENVIRONMENT FAULT: report BLOCKED, never a defect in the MCP tools.

The seed data is loaded: organization Northwharf Ltd (`10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001`) exists, with Ada's card `10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000041` (last four `4412`, seeded `spending_limit_minor` 500000).

`DATABASE_URL` is present and points at the same Postgres database the running app uses, so the flow can read the `cards` row back directly and restore the seeded limit in cleanup.

testGenerationContext:
## The user flow under test

As the owner Ada North, change a debit card limit and read the card back.

### The outcome that must hold at the end

The card's limit is the amount Ada set.

Read this back from the system in the flow's last step and assert it. A flow that only checks the status code of its last call has not tested the thing the user named.

### The endpoints it crosses, in order

1. `TOOL list_cards`
2. `TOOL set_card_limit`
3. `TOOL list_cards`

Implement one `ctx.step(...)` per entry, in this order, carrying values between them in local variables. The final entry is the endpoint the flow is ABOUT; the ones before it are setup that must succeed for it to mean anything.

### Additional guidance

Actor is the seeded owner Ada North. Mint her access token with AuthClient from @auth0/auth0-auth-js by calling getTokenByPassword. Do not POST /oauth/token by hand and do not use mintJwt. Read AUTH0_DOMAIN (localhost:3000, hostname only), AUTH0_CLIENT_ID, AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET, AUTH0_AUDIENCE, AUTH0_TEST_USERNAME, and AUTH0_TEST_PASSWORD. Authenticate in arrange, then send Authorization: Bearer on every MCP tools/call. AuthClient always requests https://AUTH0_DOMAIN. This issuer listens with HTTP on port 3000. If the token request fails for that reason, the scenario must report BLOCKED as an environment fault and must not treat it as a defect in the MCP tool. Ada's card is 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000041, last four 4412, seeded limit 500000. The first list_cards is setup. set_card_limit is the change. The second list_cards reads the new limit. Restore spending_limit_minor to 500000 in cleanup.

parameters.gapReason: this is a user flow, which emits exactly one scenario; the header is sent with the owner's valid bearer token only and no scenario varies it to a missing or invalid value
